comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ESCAPE HATCH — required, per operator direction. The goal is NO AD-HOC raw git, not 'no raw
git ever'. Tonight is the proof: the store was wedged by the stash race, every rebar write
failed, and raw git in the tracker was the ONLY way out. A hard prohibition with no sanctioned
door would have left the operator stranded with a dead ticket system.

So the design must ship BOTH halves:

(a) THE SUPPORTED DOOR — a first-class maintenance surface that performs the raw-git
    operations correctly, so nobody has to improvise them:
      - it is the ONLY blessed way to mutate the tracker outside the normal event-append path;
      - it TAKES A BACKUP REF BEFORE THE FIRST WRITE, not mid-run. (The 'pre-a3-remediation'
        tag was stamped after 2 of 4 batches and was therefore useless as a rollback point —
        that is exactly the mistake to design out.)
      - it REFUSES when unpushed local ticket commits would be lost (`rev-list
        origin/tickets..HEAD` non-empty), because that is the one condition that separates a
        recoverable local mess from actual event loss;
      - it is AUDITABLE: what ran, when, by whom, and what changed — recorded durably rather
        than living only in a shell history.

(b) THE BREAK-GLASS — an explicit, deliberately-inconvenient flag (`--force`-style, requiring
    a written reason) for the genuinely unforeseen case the supported door does not cover. It
    should be loud in the output and recorded, so a reviewer can later see it was used and why.
    Same posture AGENTS.md already takes for the claim/close gates: an escape hatch for a human
    operator's judgment call, not a routine agent move.

WHAT THIS IS NOT: a reason to keep the current situation, where agents reach for `git add -A`
/ `commit` / `merge` / `push` / `rm` in the tracker because nothing better exists. That is
what happened in this session's remediation, and it is how source files and stray state get
committed to the tickets branch.

RELATIONSHIP TO THE AUTO-HEAL AC: auto-heal removes MOST of the need for the hatch — tonight's
wedge satisfied the safe auto-heal condition (no unpushed commits) and would have self-repaired
with no human intervention at all. The hatch exists for what auto-heal deliberately refuses to
touch, i.e. the cases where events would be lost and a human must decide.

Add to the acceptance criteria:
- [ ] A supported maintenance entrypoint exists with backup-before-first-write, a refusal when
      unpushed ticket commits are present, and a durable audit record.
- [ ] A break-glass override exists for cases the supported entrypoint does not cover; it
      requires an explicit written reason and is surfaced loudly in output.
- [ ] Docs state the rule as 'no AD-HOC raw git in the tracker; use the maintenance entrypoint',
      and name the break-glass, so the guidance is actionable rather than a bare prohibition.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
AUTO-HEAL: the exact gap, and a safer rule than my earlier 'hard-reset if no unpushed commits'.

`_store/event_append.py:_recover_from_unmerged` (line ~671) ALREADY auto-heals a stranded
index — but its classifier has only TWO buckets:
    _REGENERABLE_PREFIX = '.bridge_state/'        (line 668)
    nonregen = [p for p in unmerged if not p.startswith(_REGENERABLE_PREFIX)]   (line 692)
Anything not under `.bridge_state/` is assumed to be TICKET DATA and the write is refused.

Tonight's unmerged paths were `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` and
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py`. Those are a THIRD kind the classifier has no bucket
for: files that do not belong on the tickets branch AT ALL. They are not regenerable, but they
are also emphatically not ticket data — `origin/tickets` tracks no source tree whatsoever
(verified: `ls-tree origin/tickets` returns only ticket dirs plus .bridge_state,
.gitattributes, .gitignore, .pre-commit-config.yaml, .store-compat.json, .ticket-write.lock).
So they fell into `nonregen` and wedged EVERY store write until a human intervened.

BETTER RULE (safer than my earlier suggestion of hard-resetting when no unpushed commits
exist, which discards more than necessary and needs a broader safety argument):

    An unmerged path that the tickets branch does not track, and that is not shaped like a
    ticket path, CANNOT be ticket data — so discard it exactly as the regenerable case does.

Classify FOREIGN as: not present in HEAD's tree AND not matching a ticket directory
(`^[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f-]+/`) AND not one of the known store dotfiles. That is conservative by
construction — it auto-discards only paths that provably do not belong to the store — and it
would have healed tonight's wedge with zero human involvement, while still refusing on a
genuine conflict inside real ticket data.

Keep the existing refuse-and-surface behaviour for anything that IS ticket-shaped. The point of
auto-heal is to remove the need to reach for raw git, which is what caused the collateral
damage in the first place.

Acceptance criteria to add:
- [ ] `_recover_from_unmerged` gains a FOREIGN-path bucket (not tracked on the tickets branch,
      not ticket-shaped, not a known store dotfile) that is discarded like the regenerable case.
- [ ] A genuine unmerged path INSIDE a ticket directory still refuses and surfaces.
- [ ] Held-out tests for both directions, using tonight's exact paths as the foreign fixture.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
TRACKER CONVERTED to a STANDALONE CLONE (approved maintenance window).

Before: .tickets-tracker was a LINKED WORKTREE — gitdir pointed into
/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.git/worktrees/-tickets-tracker, sharing one .git (and therefore ONE
stash stack) with 11 source worktrees. That sharing is the mechanism behind this bug.
After: .git is a real directory — own index, own refs, own stash stack (0 entries). A stash
created in any source worktree can no longer be popped into the ticket store.

This matches production: infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:154 already creates the reviewbot's
store with 'git clone --single-branch --branch tickets'. The dev machine was the outlier.

PROCEDURE (worth encoding in the maintenance entrypoint AC):
  1. rebar bridge pause '<reason>'   — durable pause, so nothing recreates the worktree
  2. quiet check: tracker HEAD stable over 20s (a writer recreated it during an earlier
     attempt and committed events mid-restructure — that attempt was aborted)
  3. verify 0 unpushed and 0 unmerged; FLUSH anything pending first (a pending
     'ticket: COMPACT' commit had to be merged + pushed before proceeding)
  4. move the worktree aside (reversible), git worktree prune
  5. clone the tickets branch STANDALONE
  6. carry over the git-ignored LOCAL store state, which a fresh clone does not have:
       .env-id (environment identity stamped into every event — MUST be preserved for
       continuity, not regenerated), .ensure-applied, .opcert-key + .opcert-key.pub (operator
       signing key, 0600), .graph-cache.json
  7. verify read AND write, then rebar bridge resume

TWO TRAPS FOUND THE HARD WAY:
  - Cloning from the LOCAL repo FAILS: this checkout is a PARTIAL (promisor) clone and cannot
    serve a full clone ('could not fetch ... from promisor remote'). Clone from the REMOTE.
    This failed with the store already moved aside, i.e. mid-outage.
  - A fresh clone is NOT a working store: writes fail with 'ticket system not initialized'
    until .env-id (and the opcert key, for signing) are carried over. Reads work fine, so the
    breakage is invisible until the first write.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: an allowlist .gitignore on the tickets branch.

Idea: replace the current denylist .gitignore with an allowlist ('/*' plus re-includes for
ticket-id dirs, jira-* dirs and the six store dotfiles) so nothing non-ticket-shaped can be
committed.

TESTED both vectors in a scratch repo rather than reasoning about it:
  A) agent runs 'git add -A' with source present  -> gitignore BLOCKS it (source not staged)
  B) 'git stash pop' from another branch          -> gitignore does NOT block it; the index
     still conflicted with 2 unmerged entries, reproducing this bug WITH the allowlist active
Reason: .gitignore governs what git auto-adds for UNTRACKED files. A stash/merge writes INDEX
entries for paths that were tracked where the stash was created, and gitignore has no
authority there. Vector B is the one that actually wedged the store.

REJECTED because it trades a LOUD failure for a SILENT one. Any future store file added at the
top level — as .store-compat.json once was — would be invisibly ignored rather than committed,
and the symptom would present as 'the feature does not work' rather than 'the file was not
tracked'. That silent-failure shape is exactly what made this session's three bugs expensive:
each was detectable but nothing was looking.

Vector A is better addressed by the maintenance entrypoint AC (agents stop needing raw git at
all) than by a branch-level trap. The wedge vector is already closed twice over: the tracker is
now a standalone clone (no shared stash stack), and the foreign-path bucket heals the index if
it ever recurs by any route.

Decision: do not add the allowlist. Recorded so it is not re-proposed.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PARTIALLY DELIVERED — change ade954fcd3 landed on main; this ticket stays OPEN.

LANDED: the self-healing AC only. gitutil.path_is_foreign_to_branch + discard_unmerged_paths,
wired into event_append._recover_from_unmerged as a third bucket. A stranded index caused by
paths the tickets branch does not track now HEALS instead of wedging every store write.

NOT LANDED — the PRIMARY AC of this ticket:
  _store/push.py STILL performs the stash -> merge -> pop dance in the tickets worktree
  (module docstring line 9; _resolve_conflicted_pop lines 167-200; 'stash drop' at line 200).
Also outstanding: the maintenance entrypoint, the break-glass, and the fsck invariant that
reports a tracker containing tracked-source paths.

RESIDUAL RISK (the reason this must not be closed):
The incident needed two conditions — (1) rebar stashes in the tickets worktree, and (2) the
stash stack contains a foreign stash. Condition 1 is STILL TRUE EVERYWHERE. Condition 2 is now
impossible ON THIS MACHINE ONLY, because .tickets-tracker was converted to a standalone clone.
Any other environment whose tracker is still a LINKED WORKTREE — which was the default setup
here — retains both conditions. The reviewbot is safe (Dockerfile.reviewbot:154 clones), but
other developer machines and CI checkouts have not been audited.

What the landed change buys everywhere: the OUTAGE is prevented (self-heal) even where the
CAUSE remains. Only the pollution still occurs.

SUBTLETY to preserve if the auto-discard is ever revisited: discarding foreign paths deletes
files that, in this incident, were a colleague's RECOVERED ADR-0061 work. That is safe ONLY
because 'git stash pop' KEEPS the stash entry when it conflicts (verified experimentally:
'The stash entry is kept in case you need it again'), so the source of truth survives and only
the applied copy is removed. If that ever ceased to hold, auto-discard would become data loss.

Suggested order for the remainder: (1) remove the stash from push.py, (2) fsck invariant so a
polluted tracker is REPORTED rather than silently healed, (3) maintenance entrypoint +
break-glass.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PRIMARY AC SHIPPED — Gerrit change 1584 (2fa6-stash-create).

WHAT LANDED
_store/push.py no longer performs ANY refs/stash mutation. The stash push -> merge ->
stash pop dance is replaced by the operator-approved design:

    sha = git stash create        # writes a stash COMMIT OBJECT, does NOT touch refs/stash
    git reset --hard -q           # create leaves the tree dirty; clear it ourselves
    git merge <target>
    git stash apply <sha>         # addresses OUR commit by sha; no stack consulted

Because the restore names a commit sha, it is unreachable from any other worktree's pop,
and there is nothing to 'stash drop' afterwards (push.py:200 is gone). Verified: no
'stash push' / 'stash pop' / 'stash drop' call sites remain in push.py.

Semantics preserved: 'stash create' records tracked modifications + index state exactly
as 'stash push' did, and neither touches untracked files; 'apply' without --index
restores unstaged, matching the old 'pop'.

AC4 (_resolve_conflicted_pop's regenerable assumption) — ENFORCED, not assumed. Renamed
to _resolve_conflicted_apply. It now classifies each conflicted path with
gitutil.path_is_foreign_to_branch and routes both buckets through
gitutil.discard_unmerged_paths: a path the tickets branch TRACKS is restored from HEAD
(reconciler rebuilds it); a path it does NOT track cannot be ticket data, so it is
removed AND logged at warning level rather than vanishing silently.

AC3 held-out test — tests/interfaces/store/test_push_shared_stash_2fa6.py. It encodes the
RACE, not the steady state: LIFO ordering alone hides the bug because an uncontended pop
does take its own push. The test injects a foreign source-worktree stash BETWEEN the
set-aside and the restore. PROVEN RED on the parent commit (origin/main push.py): the
raced stash is applied and src/raced.py materializes inside the store — the incident
reproduced. GREEN on the fix, with the shared stack left byte-identical (both foreign
entries still present, neither popped nor dropped).
It also asserts a non-conflicting dirty file returns byte-for-byte, which proves the tree
was genuinely RESTORED rather than merely reset away.

GATES: make lint clean, mypy clean (491 files), 378 store tests pass. push.py is 792 LOC
(was 758) — 8 lines under the hard cap, which is uncomfortably tight and is more evidence
for story 5e53.

STILL OPEN ON THIS TICKET (not delivered by 1584):
- fsck invariant: report a tracker containing tracked-source paths (reuse
  path_is_foreign_to_branch) so pollution is REPORTED, not only healed.
- The supported maintenance entrypoint (backup ref BEFORE the first write; REFUSE when
  rev-list origin/tickets..HEAD is non-empty; durable audit record).
- The break-glass override + the docs rule ('no AD-HOC raw git; use the entrypoint').
Do NOT close this ticket until those ship.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ALL REMAINING ACs NOW HAVE CHANGES UP FOR REVIEW. Stack: 1584 -> 1585 -> 1588.

1588 — 'rebar tracker-maintenance', the supported door (ACs 6, 7, 8):
  * BACKUP REF BEFORE THE FIRST WRITE — refs/rebar-maintenance/<utc> at current HEAD,
    printed with its rollback command. Tested: the ref must point at HEAD-BEFORE, not after.
  * REFUSAL on unpushed ticket commits (rev-list origin/tickets..HEAD non-empty). A refused
    run makes NO writes AT ALL, backup ref included — that is asserted, not assumed. It fails
    CLOSED: a missing origin/tickets also refuses, because local commits cannot then be proven
    safe. Treating 'unknowable' as zero would defeat the guard.
  * DURABLE AUDIT — actor (git identity, falling back to $USER), argv, backup ref,
    unpushed count, forced flag + reason, and the paths touched; appended as JSONL to the
    tracker's GIT DIR, deliberately not the worktree, so it can never become store content a
    later merge conflicts on.
  * BREAK-GLASS --force=<reason>: requires a written reason (bare --force is rejected exit 2),
    loud on stderr, recorded as forced:true with the reason.
  * DOCS state the rule and name the break-glass: AGENTS.md pointer, a new
    docs/concurrency.md section 'Mutating the tracker: no AD-HOC raw git', cli-reference.md
    (generated), exit-codes.md.
6 envelope tests cover the above.

DESIGN NOTE: the foreign-path classifier is single-sourced as fsck.foreign_store_path_list —
fsck renders it, tracker-maintenance ACTS on it. Two copies would be free to drift, and a
repair that disagreed with the report it was shown could delete something fsck never named.

CI FOUND TWO THINGS MY LOCAL RUN DID NOT — both real, both fixed:
  1. raw-git-write gate: its '# raw-git-ok:' marker is keyed to the CALL's own line, so
     markers placed on the preceding comment line do not count. Affected the new
     reset --hard / update-ref / rm calls. Fixed by moving each call onto its own line with
     the marker attached.
  2. docs/cli-reference.md is GENERATED; I had hand-edited it. Regenerated with
     scripts/gen_cli_reference.py, which produces a better entry than mine (it inlines the
     full help text including the safety envelope). All four generators now pass --check.

GATE STATUS: 1584 is LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1. 1585 LLM +1, CI running. 1588 re-pushed,
gates running. Ticket stays OPEN until the stack merges.

compiled_state.description:
# The ticket store must be mutated through rebar, never through git stash

`_store/push.py` performs a stash -> merge -> pop dance inside the tickets worktree (module
docstring, bug 12a6), with `_resolve_conflicted_pop` (push.py:167-200) to repair a pop that
applies with conflict (bug 6818). It ends by dropping the stash (push.py:200).

## Why the design is unsound
Its stated assumption is that "the stashed working-tree edits live on reconciler-REGENERABLE
files" (push.py:170-176). That assumption does not hold, because **git's stash stack is shared
across every worktree of a repository**. `.tickets-tracker` is a LINKED WORKTREE of
`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.git`, and this machine currently has ELEVEN worktrees on that repo.
A `git stash pop` executed in the tickets worktree can therefore pop a stash created in a
SOURCE worktree.

## Observed incident
A stash created on branch `fix-c5b3-scc-byfile` was popped into the tickets worktree:

    stash@{0}: On fix-c5b3-scc-byfile: RECOVERED measurement-provenance work
    (ADR 0061 / det_measurement_provenance) displaced into worktree fix-c5b3-scc-byfile
    by a shared-stash race; backup at /tmp/RECOVERED-stash-race

Its contents are exactly the two paths that kept conflicting in the tracker:
    .rebar/criteria_routing.json            +23
    src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py  +9
Neither is reconciler-regenerable; both are source. Effects:
- SOURCE files (src/, docs/, tests/, .rebar/) appeared in the tickets worktree, which tracks
  no source tree at all — origin/tickets is clean, so this is purely local corruption.
- The index was left with unmerged (DU) entries and NO MERGE_HEAD — a stranded state that
  blocks EVERY ticket write. It oscillated (4 unmerged -> 0 -> 4) as concurrent rebar
  operations popped and re-stashed, so manual cleanup did not hold.
- It blocked the close of bug beb1 whose completion verification had already PASSED, and
  caused two COMPLETION_VERDICT sidecars to be lost ("could not be written").
- The stash message records that this race had ALREADY displaced work once before.

## Principle
The ticket system is an event-sourced store with its own API. It must be mutated through
rebar, not by direct filesystem/git manipulation of the tracker worktree. `git stash` in
particular is a REPO-GLOBAL operation being used for worktree-local intent, which is the
category error here.

(For the record: agents have also been doing direct git in the tracker — this session used
`git add -A` / `commit` / `merge` / `push` / `rm` there during a remediation. That is the same
violation from the other direction and should also be designed out, e.g. a locked
commit-and-push entrypoint that agents use instead.)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] rebar performs NO `git stash` operation in the tickets worktree. Replace the
      stash->merge->pop dance with a mechanism that cannot touch a shared, repo-global stack —
      e.g. commit-then-merge on the tickets branch, a worktree-scoped temporary ref, or a
      `git -c stash.useBuiltin` free path that stages into a dedicated ref.
- [ ] If any stash-like step is unavoidable, it must be provably scoped so it can never apply
      a stash entry created by another worktree/branch (assert the stash's branch-of-origin
      before popping, and refuse otherwise).
- [ ] Held-out test: with an unrelated stash created on a DIFFERENT branch of the same repo,
      a tickets-store write that hits the push-retry path must not apply it and must not
      strand the index.
- [ ] `_resolve_conflicted_pop`'s regenerable-files assumption is either enforced or removed.
- [ ] fsck (or the store write path) reports a tickets worktree containing tracked-source
      paths, since origin/tickets legitimately has none.
compiled_state.title: rebar must not use git stash in the tickets worktree — the stash stack is shared across all worktrees
